projects.heading: A few things I've somehow managed to ship.
projects.desc: Not an exhaustive list, but a few highlights. From crypto-native flows to the world's most basic todo app.

sidebar.lightModeToast2: We don't do light mode here. It attracts bugs.

hero.headline2: Once spent 3 hours debugging a semicolon issue.
hero.headline3: Have deployed on Friday. Have survived. Mostly.
hero.headline4: Self-hosts everything. Ends up paying more.
hero.lede: Senior Frontend Developer · 5+ years of experience of centering div. I write code that occasionally does what I want. Specialized in turning Figma designs into 'close enough' implementations.

about.bio1: Started in mobile with Flutter — one codebase, two platforms, mild despair. Ten months later I moved to Flutter-for-web. Yes, that's a thing. No, I don't want to talk about it.
about.bio2: Eventually found Vue and Nuxt and never looked back, partly out of love, partly because Flutter-for-web is behind me and I refuse to make eye contact. (Please stop asking about it).
about.bio3: These days I ship complex web apps and crypto-native flows: WalletConnect pairings that pair on the second try, MetaMask sign-in that doesn't popup, on-chain reads & writes, and a checkout flow with the lowest (highest) gas fee you can ever imagine.
about.bio4: Off-clock: a homelab running Jellyfin + the *arr stack + Immich, all docker-compose'd behind Tailscale — works flawlessly until it doesn't, then works again (Nothing a hard reset can't fix). Also a Claude + n8n + Obsidian pipeline that reads the internet for me, so I can spend that saved time on… more internet.

entry1.bullet1: First year: Flutter, but for the web. (Yes, that exists.)
entry1.bullet2: Transitioned to Nuxt + Pinia + Tailwind — the daily tools now.
entry1.bullet3: Shipped Web3 flows: WalletConnect, MetaMask, smart-contract calls.
entry1.bullet4: Crypto checkout, on-chain actions, wallet UX that doesn't scare normies.

entry2.bullet1: Built mobile apps in Flutter — iOS + Android from one codebase.
entry2.bullet2: Ten months. The classic first-job arc.

homelab.heading: Self-hosted, all of it.
homelab.p1: {service} stack for media, because subscribing to 10 million different streaming services is so fun!
homelab.p2: {service} for every photo — I'm not paying Apple a single cent.
homelab.p3: {service} for extra automation, so I can collect my favourite memes and watch them offline.
homelab.p4: All {compose}, fronted by {vpn} — no port-forwarding theatre.

ai.desc: Three tools I use to read the internet without drowning in it. They happen to work well together — but each pulls its weight on its own.
ai.n8nDesc: Self-hosted automation that schedules and routes. Pulls RSS feeds, newsletters, and pages, so I can spend more time online...offline.
ai.n8nSolo: Useful on its own for any repeatable task you'd otherwise do by hand.
ai.claudeDesc: Hey Claude, fix it for me. Make no mistakes.
ai.claudeSolo: Useful on its own as a thinking partner, code reviewer, or research assistant.
ai.obsidianDesc: Linked everything I need to remember, because I don't even remember what I had for breakfast.
ai.obsidianSolo: Useful on its own as a personal wiki, journal, or second brain.

contact.heading: Say hi! But like with text. Don't actually call me.
